clinician.trajectory_summary: A 74-year-old male presented in 2005 with a one-year history of pruritic, erythematous plaque and cord-like nodular lesions on his left thigh and leg. Initial histopathology and culture results were not reported. A skin biopsy was later performed and histopathology showed hyperkeratosis, epidermal acanthosis, a predominantly lymphohistiocytic infiltrate including giant cells and hemosiderin-laden histiocytes. Grocott's methenamine silver stain revealed numerous thick-walled round yeasts occurring singly or in chains connected by tubular projections, characteristic of lobomycosis. No culture or molecular confirmation was documented. No further clinical course or treatment response data were available.
